title: Response time vs Burn-rate sampler (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Quick sketch of an experiment comparing user-visible response time envelopes against per-request burn rate (dollars burned) across three runtime shapes. Goal: produce a short collateral piece (for Console + Optimize) that helps product decide which knob combinations to surface to developers (batching, slotization, and prewarm) and an internal recommendation for default presets. This is a working doc — rough numbers, approximations, and open questions noted.

Motivation / product framing
---
- Developers ask: how much faster will my p95 get if I accept X% more spend?
- We currently surface separate charts for latency percentiles and cost but not a combined time-to-response vs burn-rate tradeoff.
- Want one-page dev-friendly chart: x-axis = median response time (ms), y-axis = cost per 1000 requests (USD) with p50/p95/p99 bands annotated.

Experiment matrix (short)
---
Workloads: chat-turn (short response ~40 tokens), assistant-long (200 tokens), embeddings (512-dim no-decoding) 
Runtimes tested: hosted-fastpath (multiplexed small-slot), dedicated-tiling (reserved GPUs with prewarm), dedicated-prefetch (tiling + KV-prefetch profile)
Knobs: batching: small (window 5ms), medium (20ms), large (100ms); prewarm: on/off; quant profile: fp16 vs q4f16
Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), throughput (qps), cost-per-1k-requests ($), energy proxy (GPU-util*ms normalized)

Representative results (approx, rough)
---
ASCII table (median numbers from runs on us-west-2 nodes):

| runtime             | batch | prewarm | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | qps  | $/1k req |
|---------------------|-------|---------|---------|---------|---------|------|---------|
| hosted-fastpath     | small | off     | 48      | 172     | 420     | 140  | 3.1     |
| hosted-fastpath     | medium| off     | 62      | 210     | 500     | 220  | 2.6     |
| dedicated-tiling    | small | on      | 38      | 115     | 240     | 180  | 4.8     |
| dedicated-tiling    | large | on      | 55      | 140     | 300     | 340  | 3.7     |
| dedicated-prefetch  | medium| on      | 42      | 120     | 260     | 240  | 3.9     |

Interpretation notes
---
- For p50-focused workloads (short interactive turns), the dedicated prewarm path yields best median latency (38–42ms) but at higher $/1k compared to hosted tuned for throughput.
- Larger batching (100ms window) drives cost down per request by ~20–30% vs small-window, but p99 suffers noticeably. Good for throughput-first embedding workloads.
- Hosted-fastpath with medium batching gives a sweet spot: modest p95 (~210ms) at low $/1k (approx $2.6). Suggests a default preset for self-serve users who want low cost and are tolerant of p95 in the low hundreds.

ASCII scatter (time vs burn-rate, conceptual)
---
(cost on Y, median latency on X; each bullet is a runtime+knob)
0.5 |                                * hosted-medium
    |                       * hosted-small
    |      * dedicated-large
0.3 | * dedicated-prefetch
    |
0.1 +--------------------------------------------
      20   60   100  140   180  220  260 300  (ms)

Rough rule-of-thumb we derived
---
- Reducing median latency by ~20–25ms typically increases burn-rate by ~10–30% depending on slotization and prewarm (large variability).
- Improving p99 below 200ms often requires moving to reserved/dedicated prewarm with spotty cost efficiency unless you accept aggressive packing across tenants.

Micro-annotations for Console UI
---
- Proposed single compact widget: 2D scatter + selectable percentile band (p50/p95/p99). Hover shows knob combo and estimated $/1k.
- Default presets: 
  - "Cost-saving" = hosted-fastpath, medium batch, prewarm=off
  - "Balanced" = dedicated-prefetch, medium batch, prewarm=on
  - "Low tail" = dedicated-tiling, small batch, prewarm=on
- Add a small "Why this matters" tooltip: short bullet about tail risk and user experience for interactive apps.

Open questions / things to validate
---
- Variability across regions — these numbers are us-west-2 only. Need eu-west-1 run.
- Multi-tenant noise: how repeatable are p99 improvements if multiple customers use prewarm simultaneously?
- Long-run cost models: these per-1k numbers ignore reserved contract amortization (Dedicated monthly commit). Recompute for monthly-CU amortization.
- Embedding workloads behave differently; separate chart needed (decoding vs encode-only).

Next steps (short)
---
- Run same matrix in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 (owner: Tomás) — target complete by 2028-06-27.
- Add monthly amortized cost column for Dedicated SKU variants (owner: Lina) — explore 3 commit levels (small/medium/large).
- Prototype Console scatter widget with percentile toggle (owner: Marco) — include hover text and presets.

Notes to self (raw)
---
- Numbers are noisy; include shaded uncertainty in final collateral.
- Consider adding a simple SLA calculator linked from Console: if you want p95 < X ms, recommended preset = Y, estimated incremental $/1k = Z.
- Crosslink to INF-4125 for telemetry tagging and to runtime PR #842 for batching change notes.

End of draft.
